changelog:
**YouTube answers in your language now.** Every request the plugin made said `hl=en, gl=US`, written into two files - so a German household read an English schedule for videos that have perfectly good German titles. YouTube localises a title and hands back the original where there is no translation, so asking in German costs nothing and loses nothing. It follows the language the configuration page is set to, and there is a field on Server settings - **Ask YouTube in** - that takes any language tag.

**An advert nobody named is called what YouTube calls it**, not `aqz-KE-bpKQ`. The title arrives on the same answer as the length, so it costs no extra request.

A test now fails the build if any code asks YouTube in a hard-coded language again.
description: Lightweight virtual TV channels: deterministic schedules over your own library, tuned in via normal direct playback at the live position. No transcoding, no tuner emulation.
name: LiteTV Channels
overview: TV channels from your library, without transcoding.
